evaluation_metrics.reasoning: RMSE penalizes large errors more heavily than MAE. In aviation, a large RUL prediction error is more dangerous than a small one — so RMSE is the right primary metric. MAE gives average error magnitude. R2 shows how much variance the model explains.

dataset_split_strategy.reasoning: Splitting by engine ID ensures no engine appears in both train and validation sets. Row-wise splitting would cause leakage as the same engine would appear in both train and test.

models_to_test.reason: Tests whether ensemble methods improve over linear baseline
Tests gradient boosting with built-in regularization
Tests whether hyperparameter tuning further improves performance

success_criteria.reasoning: R2 above 0.75 indicates model explains at least 75 percent of RUL variance — acceptable for predictive maintenance. RMSE below 20 cycles means predictions are within 20 flight cycles of actual RUL — operationally acceptable for scheduling.
